newsitem.title: UK: IPE trade just firmer, trapped in eight cent range.
newsitem.headline: IPE trade just firmer, trapped in eight cent range.

text.p: IPE Brent crude oil futures were little changed in very thin business, traders and brokers said.

September Brent crude, the new front month, was trading at $18.33 a barrel at 1145 GMT, a gain of three cents on the day. The contract has been trapped in a range between $18.26 and $18.34 since the market opened.
August gas oil was 25 cents a tonne firmer at $164, after moving in a narrow 75-cent range.
"There is absolutely nothing new out there," one dealer said.
Players in the market were waiting for fresh signs of possible renewed Iraqi exports.

The U.N. confirmed late on Wednesday that Iraq will not be allowed to carry more than five percent of its $1 billion allowance over into the second 90-day tranche of a current six-month, $2 billion oil-for-food sales deal, which came into effect on June 8.

Because of delays in lifting Iraqi crude so far this means the $1 billion worth of oil will have to be squeezed into a much shorter time period, which could mean exports of over 1.5 million barrels per day in August or early September.
In Nigeria, Shell said it had reopened 12 flow stations which were shut after a fire last week, which took out about 135,000 barrels of lost production.
